b.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)

edges.label: AATIP's 2017 disclosure pulled a Vanderbilt lab into UAP research
edges.note: Bruehl, a professor of Anesthesiology at Vanderbilt whose primary field is pain research, told his own institution that the December 2017 New York Times report revealing AATIP is what restarted his interest: 'My interest, honestly, has gone up and gone down over the years, and prior to 2017, I had kind of gotten bored with it and didn't really pay much attention to it. But the report in The New York Times got me thinking again.' What followed was a methodological judgement rather than a belief: 'That's when I realized that nobody's really studying this scientifically.'

b.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)

edges.label: Vanderbilt UAP statistician invited to a Pentagon-sponsored expert meeting
edges.note: Vanderbilt University Medical Center reports that Stephen Bruehl, PhD, professor of Anesthesiology, 'was invited to attend a Pentagon-sponsored meeting for discussions with UAP experts from the government and academia' in August 2025, as his cluster analysis of 216 well-documented UAP cases (1947-2016) neared publication in World Futures. The sponsoring office is not named in the source.
